## What it is

- The **Fuzz Face** came out in **1966**, made by **Arbiter** in London (Wikipedia, "Fuzz Face").
- Two knobs: **Volume** and **Fuzz**. A round metal case with a footswitch.
- Early ones used **germanium** transistors; from the late 1960s **silicon**, which Wikipedia says sounded harsher.

## How it makes its sound

- Two transistors give a lot of gain. The signal hits the top and bottom of what they can put out: the wave is squared off (**clipped**), which adds many new harmonics.
- The clipping is not the same on top and bottom (*asymmetric*): that adds even harmonics too. In this page's model a bias does that (the site's reading of germanium fuzz).
- Its input takes a lot of current from the guitar: a **low input impedance**, about 5-8 kΩ (ElectroSmash, from a search summary). So the guitar's own volume knob changes the sound: at 10, the pickup loses treble into that load; turned down, the knob's resistance isolates the pickup, less signal reaches the transistors and the fuzz **cleans up** (Wikipedia).
- Put it first in the chain: after another pedal, that pedal drives it and the clean-up trick is gone (this page models that).

## The pedal

The Fuzz Face's face, drawn after photos (positions approximate, no logos). Drag a knob (or use the arrow keys), click the footswitch to bypass, then press a ▶ button. The guitar is this site's pickup model (pick one, and its volume, below the buttons); the sound goes through the pedal model, then a clean amp. Nobody has compared it with a real pedal. The picture shows the waveform going in and coming out.

## Guided tour

```{=html}
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="fuzzface" data-set="{&quot;fuzz&quot;:9,&quot;vol&quot;:7,&quot;gvol&quot;:10}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Fuzz 9, guitar volume 10.</b> Thick, squared-off fuzz.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="fuzzface" data-set="{&quot;fuzz&quot;:9,&quot;vol&quot;:7,&quot;gvol&quot;:6}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Same pedal, guitar volume 6.</b> Listen: much cleaner, brighter. Nothing on the pedal changed.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="fuzzface" data-set="{&quot;fuzz&quot;:9,&quot;vol&quot;:7,&quot;gvol&quot;:4}" data-play="chord"><p><b>Guitar volume 4.</b> Nearly clean chords.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="fuzzface" data-set="{&quot;fuzz&quot;:3,&quot;vol&quot;:8,&quot;gvol&quot;:10}" data-play="riff"><p><b>Fuzz 3.</b> Less gain: a gritty crunch.</p></div>
<div class="pd-step" data-pedal="fuzzface" data-set="{&quot;fuzz&quot;:10,&quot;vol&quot;:6,&quot;gvol&quot;:10}" data-play="lead"><p><b>Fuzz 10.</b> Long sustain on a lead line.</p></div>
```
